name: PresentationSpace
tagline: Office-style slide editing in C#, one engine for browser and desktop
summary: PresentationSpace is an Office-style presentation workspace built with Uno Platform and SkiaSharp, with a tabbed ribbon, filmstrip, notes, slide sorter and slide show. The browser runs the same .NET application compiled to WebAssembly, not an HTML mock-up. Underneath sits an independent, reusable engine for immutable documents, rich text, merged tables, native charts and a documented PPTX subset, plus PNG and vector PDF export.

highlights.title: Familiar ribbon workspace
highlights.text: Home, Insert, Draw, Design, Transitions, Animations, Slide Show, Review, View, Shape Format, Table Design and Help tabs, plus the File workspace.

highlights.title: Direct Skia canvas
highlights.text: The editor viewport, slide previews and player draw straight onto Uno's SKCanvasElement compositor canvas, with retained drawing and picture caches.

highlights.title: Mixed rich text
highlights.text: Character styles, bullets, paragraph alignment and spacing survive editing, native files, supported PPTX interchange and PNG/PDF export.

highlights.title: Merged, styled tables
highlights.text: Merge and split cells, insert or delete tracks, and apply Table Design palette presets, banding and ten border scopes.

highlights.title: Native charts
highlights.text: Six categorical chart types with multi-series data, exported as native chart parts with editable embedded XLSX workbooks.

highlights.title: PPTX interchange
highlights.text: Import and export a documented PPTX subset: text runs, preset shapes, pictures, tables, charts, notes and basic transitions.

highlights.title: Slide show
highlights.text: Present from the beginning or current slide with fade/push/wipe transitions, appear/fade/fly-in effects and black or white screen.

highlights.title: Deck-scale virtualization
highlights.text: Virtualized filmstrip and sorter views recycle only visible tiles; open the 1,000-slide sample to try it.

items: New, duplicate, delete, reorder and hide slides
Non-destructive predefined layouts that retain unmatched content
Backgrounds, slide sizing and slide numbers
Resizable filmstrip and slide sorter
Text, basic geometric shapes, lines/arrows and raster pictures
Multi-selection, marquee, eight resize handles and rotation
Aspect constraints, snapping, nudging, pan and zoom
Selection groups, front/back ordering, alignment and distribution
Object locking and visibility
Mixed character styles with bold, italic and underline on selected ranges
Bullets, paragraph alignment and spacing
Wrapping and vertical alignment
Find and replace that preserves styles between matches
Rectangular merges and splits, row/column insertion and deletion
Cell fills, margins and solid/dashed/dotted borders
Table Design: four palette presets, first/last-column emphasis and column banding
Ten border scopes that update both sides of shared edges
Up to 100 rows, 100 columns and one million characters per table
Column, bar, line, area, pie and doughnut charts
Multi-series data with nullable values and grouping options
Standalone chart data editor with spreadsheet copy/paste
Native chart parts with editable embedded XLSX workbooks on PPTX export
Basic fade, push and wipe transitions
Appear, fade and fly-in object effects
Hidden-slide skipping and black/white screen
Present from the beginning (F5) or current slide (Shift+F5)
Transactional undo/redo and an internal clipboard
Command search with Alt+Q
Speaker notes and local comments

Bounded ZIP/XML input checks: DTDs prohibited, no external-relationship retrieval

playground.intro: The live build is the same .NET editor compiled to WebAssembly, so you can build, format and present a deck right in the browser with no account or server.

tour.title: Scale up to 1,000 slides
tour.text: Use Open large-deck sample to load a 1,000-slide workspace, scroll the filmstrip, and open Rendering statistics for draw and cache counters.

tour.title: Format mixed text
tour.text: Double-click a text box (or press F2), select a few words and press Ctrl+B or Ctrl+I; the slide canvas shows the mixed styling after commit.

tour.title: Switch layouts safely
tour.text: Press Alt+Q and run Apply Title only layout, then Apply Blank layout; unmatched content is retained rather than deleted.

tour.title: Build a chart
tour.text: Search Edit chart data to change values, then try Chart type Doughnut or Chart grouping Stacked from command search.

tour.title: Design a table
tour.text: Select a table, open Format Shape → Table design & layout, then use the Table Design tab for palette presets, banding and borders.

tour.title: Present it
tour.text: Press F5 to start the slide show, use the arrows or Space to navigate, B or W for a black or white screen, and Esc to end.

architecture.name: Document model
architecture.text: Immutable documents, slides, shapes, rich text, tables and charts with an EditorSession command boundary and bounded undo.

architecture.name: Formats and rendering
architecture.text: Dependency-free PPTX import/export alongside a SkiaSharp renderer for the canvas, thumbnails, PNG and vector PDF.

architecture.name: Uno controls
architecture.text: An Office-style ribbon plus slide viewport, filmstrip, sorter, inspectors, data editors and slide show controls.

architecture.name: Editor
architecture.text: The complete embeddable editing workspace, with storage injected through IWorkspaceStorage.

boundaries: Development preview: not a complete or pixel-exact PowerPoint implementation
PPTX import is not lossless: unsupported OOXML parts are dropped, so keep the original file
AutoSave is device-local recovery only, not cloud backup or coauthoring
Inline text input is a plain TextBox; mixed styling appears on the canvas after commit
SmartArt, media, full master/theme inheritance, second-display presenter view and .ppt/.pptm remain unfinished
